Key audit matter:
Valuation of unquoted investments
The Group has applied valuation techniques to determine the fair
value of unquoted equity investments. These valuation techniques
utilize significant unobservable inputs.
A change to the techniques or assumptions used in the valuation
could produce significantly different valuation outcomes.
Due to their significance to the financial statements and the
judgments involved, the valuation of unquoted equity investments
was considered to be a key audit matter.
Further details on the Group’s unquoted investments are set out in
Note 17.
How our audit addressed the matter:
We performed, among others, the following procedures:
• Testing the design and operating effectiveness of the Group’s
controls over the valuation of unquoted investments
• Obtained an understanding of valuation techniques used
by management and compared them to generally accepted
valuation practices
• Comparing the key inputs and assumptions in the valuation
workings to supporting documentation including independently
obtained data. Where inputs included forecast financial
information, we compared the forecasts to historical financial
information.
• Tested the mathematical accuracy of the valuation workings
